recent_articles.title: Congress leader Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan elected Kerala Speaker - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan**, a senior Congress leader, was elected as the Speaker of the 16th Kerala Legislative Assembly on Friday (May 22, 2026). He won with 101 votes, defeating **A.C. Moideen** and **B.B. Gopakumar**.  The election took place after **G. Sudhakaran**, the previous Pro Tem Speaker, chose not to vote.  **V.D. Satheesan**, the Chief Minister, and **Pinarayi Vijayan**, the Leader of the Opposition, led Radhakrishnan to the Speaker's chair.

recent_articles.title: ASHAs meet Kerala CM-designate V.D. Satheesan, urge him to honour pre-poll promises - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kerala ASHA Health Workers’ Association (KAHWA)** met with **V.D. Satheesan**, the new Chief Minister-designate, to reiterate their demands for an increase in honorarium and retirement benefits. They expressed hope that the new government would prioritize addressing their concerns.  **Satheesan** assured them that he would not forget his pre-election promise of resolving their grievances.

recent_articles.title: Watch: Congress ends suspense: V. D. Satheesan to be next Kerala CM | Above the Fold | 14.05.2026 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kerala Congress** named V.D. Satheesan as its new Chief Minister after weeks of internal discussions, ending months of uncertainty.  The **BRICS Foreign Ministers’ meeting**, hosted by India in New Delhi, saw **External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar** address key global challenges and diplomatic priorities.

recent_articles.title: Kerala CM announcement LIVE: Congress names V.D. Satheesan as Kerala CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **AICC** announced **V.D. Satheesan** as the Chief Minister designate of Kerala, ending a ten-day period of uncertainty following the May 4th election results. The announcement was made by **Ajay Maken**, **Mukul Wasnik**, and **Deepa Dasmunshi** at the AICC Office.  The Congress will now proceed to form the government in the state after securing the majority.

recent_articles.title: ‘Bangla Pokkho’ founder Garga Chatterjee arrested for spreading EVM misinformation - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Garga Chatterjee**, founder of the pro-Bengali advocacy organization **Bangla Pokkho**, was arrested by the **Kolkata Police** on Tuesday for allegedly spreading misinformation about EVM manipulation during the recent West Bengal Assembly elections. The arrest followed a complaint filed by the District Election Officer of Kolkata North and comes after Mr. Chatterjee's previous arrest in 2022 for alleged community-based hate speech.  Former Trinamool Congress Minister **Sujit Bose** was also sent to 10-day ED custody on Tuesday, accused of illegally recommending candidates for South Dum Dum Municipality positions in exchange for financial benefits. Newly appointed West Bengal Sports Minister **Nisith Pramanik** has requested the file related to the Lionel Messi event in Kolkata and plans to take action if necessary.

recent_articles.title: BJP MLA Tapas Roy sworn in as Pro-tem Speaker of West Bengal Assembly - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tapas Roy**, a senior Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader and MLA from Maniktala, was sworn in as the Pro-Tem Speaker of the West Bengal Assembly on Tuesday, May 12, 2026. **Suvendu Adhikari**, the Chief Minister, attended the ceremony. The oath-taking of other MLAs will be held on Wednesday and Thursday, with the election for Speaker scheduled for Friday.

recent_articles.title: CPI(M) defends Vijayan, says leadership is collective after Kerala defeat - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **M.A. Baby**, **CPI(M)** general secretary, stated that **Pinarayi Vijayan** cannot be solely held responsible for the Left Democratic Front's (LDF) loss in Kerala. He emphasized that the party functions as a collective unit and that **Vijayan** led the campaign as its senior-most member.  Baby did not specify who within the LDF will assume the Leader of the Opposition position, despite widespread speculation about **Vijayan** potentially holding it.

recent_articles.title: Kerala’s fiscal worries - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **V.D. Satheesan**, the **Kerala** Opposition Leader, claims that the newly elected **UDF** government inherited a nearly empty treasury from the **LDF**.  The new government faces challenges in managing Kerala's finances, including high expenditures on salaries, pensions, and interest payments, limited tax revenue potential, and the impact of the 16th Finance Commission awards. The outgoing Finance Minister, **K.N. Balagopal**, disputes these claims, emphasizing that the state is in a better financial position than it was under the previous government.  The new government will need to address these challenges to fulfill its promises of development and social welfare programs.

recent_articles.title: Suvendu Adhikari | The Bengal pivot - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, a prominent Trinamool Congress leader, defected to the **BJP** in December 2020 after several senior party members attempted to persuade him to stay.  Adhikari's decision was driven by his ambition to become West Bengal's Chief Minister, an aspiration he felt unattainable within the **Trinamool Congress**. His departure came as a significant blow to the party, especially with the emergence of **Abhishek Banerjee**, Mamata Banerjee's nephew, who had gained prominence in the political landscape.

recent_articles.title: Kerala CM debate: Kharge to hold crucial talks with senior leaders today evening - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mallikarjun Kharge**, **AICC president**, will meet with key figures in the Kerala Congress leadership, including **K.C. Venugopal**, **V.D. Satheesan**, and **Ramesh Chennithala**, on Saturday (May 9, 2026) to discuss the selection of a new Chief Minister.  **Rahul Gandhi** is expected to meet with the Kerala leaders after a consensus emerges from the meeting chaired by **Kharge**.

recent_articles.title: M.A. Baby dismisses DMK-AIADMK alliance rumours, urges Governor to invite TVK to form government - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **M.A. Baby**, general secretary of the **Communist Party of India (Marxist)**, dismissed claims that the **DMK** and **AIADMK** were planning to form a government in Tamil Nadu.  He stated that the people's mandate favored the **Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)**, which emerged as the single-largest party in the 2026 Assembly elections, despite falling short of a majority.

recent_articles.title: Which party governs which State/UT: In maps - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** and its allies secured victories in Assam, Puducherry, and West Bengal, while the Congress-led UDF won in Tamil Nadu. **Suvendu Adhikari**, a BJP leader, is set to become the first BJP Chief Minister of West Bengal. The results mark a shift in the political landscape with the BJP or the NDA now governing 20 states and 2 Union Territories.

recent_articles.title: Final decision on Kerala CM turns into political cliff-hanger as ball now in Congress High Command’s court - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Congress** party in Kerala is facing uncertainty regarding the selection of its Chief Minister, with three potential candidates – **V.D. Satheesan**, **K.C. Venugopal**, and **Ramesh Chennithala** – vying for the position.  The decision appears to be pending a final announcement from the **Congress High Command**, who are reportedly meeting with the contenders in Delhi on Saturday.

recent_articles.title: Tamil Nadu government formation: CPI, CPI(M) extend unconditional support to TVK; VCK may follow suit - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **C. Joseph Vijay**, leader of the **Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)**, is seeking to form a government in Tamil Nadu after receiving support from the **Communist Party of India** and **CPI(Marxist)**.  The VCK remains undecided on backing the TVK, while **T.T.V. Dhinakaran**, leader of the **Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam (AMMK)**, has accused his party's lone MLA-elect of forging a letter of support for the TVK. The Governor is yet to issue a decision on the request for forming the government, with the possibility of President’s Rule looming if no government is formed by May 10th.

recent_articles.title: Kerala election results: Congress high command to pick Kerala CM; most UDF allies for Satheesan - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Congress Legislative Party** in Kerala authorized the party high command to choose the next Chief Minister after a resolution was passed.  **AICC** observers, **Mukul Wasnik**, **Ajay Maken**, and **Deepa Dasmunsi**, met with all 63 legislators to gauge their preferences for the position. The three frontrunners in the race are former Leader of Opposition **V.D. Satheesan**, **K.C. Venugopal**, and **Ramesh Chennithala**.  **UDF** allies, including the **IUML**, have indicated support for **Satheesan**, while **KPCC** president **Sunny Joseph** has called for a decision based on public sentiment. The observers will present their findings to the high command, who is expected to make a final call soon.

recent_articles.title: Kerala CM to be chosen by Congress High Command is acceptable for CMP, says C.P. John - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **C. P. John**, general secretary of the **Communist Marxist Party (CMP)**, stated that the party would accept the **Congress High Command's** chosen Kerala Chief Minister.  He also acknowledged the possibility of a ministerial berth for the CMP but declined to comment further. **John** expressed gratitude to voters and noted the CMP's historical performance in Kannur despite a decline in its overall vote base. He emphasized addressing the potable water crisis in Thiruvananthapuram as his immediate priority.

recent_articles.title: Left parties, VCK hold the key as DMK discusses idea of an AIADMK coalition - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **DMK** president M.K. Stalin invited **CPI(M)** State secretary P. Shanmugam, **CPI** State secretary M. Veerapandian, and **VCK** leader Thol. Thirumavalavan to discuss a potential DMK-backed AIADMK government. The Left parties have six MLAs and are crucial for forming the government with 118 seats required. While the DMK is considering supporting an AIADMK government from outside, its allies will decide on joining such a coalition.

recent_articles.title: 65% of newly elected Bengal MLAs face criminal cases; 61% are ‘crorepatis’: ADR - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR)** reported that 65% of newly elected legislators in the **West Bengal Assembly** have declared criminal cases, a significant increase from previous elections.  Of these, 58% face serious charges, including murder and attempt to murder. The report also found that 74% of winning candidates from the **Bharatiya Janata Party** and 43% from the **All India Trinamool Congress** have declared criminal cases.  The total assets of all winning candidates stand at ₹1,091 crore, with an average asset of Rs 3.73 crore per MLA. The report also highlighted concerns about the rising wealth among elected representatives and under-representation of women in the legislature.

recent_articles.title: ​Back in the saddle: On the Congress win in the Kerala Assembly polls - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Congress**-led **United Democratic Front (UDF)** won a landslide victory in the Kerala state assembly elections, ending 10 years of opposition. The UDF capitalized on anti-incumbency sentiment against the **CPI(M)**-led **Left Democratic Front (LDF)** and secured 102 seats.  The **BJP** made gains, securing three seats while drawing a substantial share of votes in various regions. The LDF faced criticism for its governance, with some accusing it of nepotism and overbearing leadership.

recent_articles.title: North Kerala districts could get fair representation in UDF Cabinet - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **UDF** is expected to form a Cabinet in the coming week, with high chances of representation for six districts in north Kerala.  The **Congress**, **IUML**, and two Independents secured 21 candidates each from Kasaragod, Wayanad, Kannur, Kozhikode, Malappuram, and Palakkad districts. Several prominent figures within the **Congress** and other parties are potential nominees for ministerial positions, including **Sunny Joseph**, **K.K. Shailaja**, and **A.P. Anil Kumar**.

recent_articles.title: Kerala polls: Congress-led UDF won not due to any individual’s efforts but as people were fed up, says NSS general secretary - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **G. Sukumaran Nair**, general secretary of the **Nair Service Society (NSS)**, stated that the Congress-led UDF's victory in the 2026 Kerala Assembly polls was due to public dissatisfaction with the government and not individual efforts by anyone, including **V.D. Satheesan**.  **Mr. Nair** attributed the Left's loss to internal issues within the party, not anti-incumbency sentiment. While acknowledging differences with **Satheesan**, he emphasized that these were not used against him during the election and asserted that the NSS did not dictate support for any candidate.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: CPI, Kerala Congress (M) suffer electoral drubbing in Ernakulam - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Communist Party of India (CPI)** and **Kerala Congress (M)** experienced electoral losses in the Ernakulam district Assembly elections.  **Mathew Kuzhalnadan** of the **Congress** defeated **N. Arun** of the CPI in Muvattupuzha, while **V. D Satheesan** of the **Congress** defeated **E.T. Taison** of the CPI in Paravur. The decline in votes for both parties was attributed to anti-incumbency factors and consolidation of minority votes towards the **United Democratic Front (UDF)**.  The results reflected a broader trend of the Left front's performance declining in the state.

recent_articles.title: Results signal political shift in Kannur, says Sunny Joseph - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **KPCC** president Sunny Joseph criticized the **CPI(M)**'s performance in the Payyannur Assembly election, calling it a "major setback" for the party. He attributed the loss to public discontent with the government and urged introspection from the leadership and cadre.  Joseph suggested that the developments could lead to further political shifts in the future.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: Payyannur verdict endorses internal criticism, signals shift in CPI(M) stronghold, says V Kunhikrishnan - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **V. Kunhikrishnan**, an independent candidate, won the Payyannur constituency in Kerala, defeating the incumbent CPI(M) candidate by a significant margin. He attributed his victory to voter support and acknowledged a broader anti-incumbency sentiment across the state. **Kunhikrishnan** stated that the results indicated a need for the **CPI(M)** leadership to introspect and make corrective actions, though he did not specify what those actions should be.  He plans to focus on developing Payyannur and will consider forming a broader platform for dissenting voices in the future.

recent_articles.title: Assembly Election 2026 results LIVE: TN, Kerala, West Bengal head into Govt formation mode - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mamata Banerjee**, **M.K. Stalin**, and **Pinarayi Vijayan** have lost their respective elections, paving the way for new governments in **Tamil Nadu**, **West Bengal**, and **Kerala**. The BJP secured a landslide victory in West Bengal, while **Vijay**'s TVK party emerged as the single-largest party in Tamil Nadu.  The saffron party also retained Assam and will be part of the incumbent NDA government in Puducherry.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: Clean sweep for UDF in Ernakulam as LDF falls flat - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The United Democratic Front (UDF)** won all 14 constituencies in Ernakulam district, marking the **Left Democratic Front's (LDF)** worst defeat in the area in over a decade.  Five segments that previously supported the LDF shifted their allegiance to the UDF, including Kalamassery, Kunnathunad, Kochi, Vypeen, and Kothamangalam. The **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)**'s alliance partner, **Twenty20**, failed to make a significant impact on the election results despite securing most seats in the district.

recent_articles.title: What the winner must learn from the loser in Kerala: No leader is inevitable - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **United Democratic Front** won the Kerala state elections, defeating the **Communist Party of India (Marxist)-led Left Democratic Front**.  The UDF's victory highlights the voters' preference for collaborative leadership over a singular figurehead. The LDF campaign focused heavily on **Pinarayi Vijayan**, its sole face, while the UDF emphasized teamwork and unity among its leaders. This approach resonated with voters who felt the LDF had become too centralized under Vijayan's rule, leading to dissatisfaction within the party itself.

recent_articles.title: ​Lost and found: The Hindu Editorial on the 2026 Assembly elections - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The 2026 Assembly elections in Assam, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Puducherry resulted in significant shifts in India's political landscape. The BJP secured victories in Assam and Puducherry while the Congress suffered its worst performance in Assam. In West Bengal, the BJP capitalized on long-term planning and a tainted election process to achieve a decisive victory.  The TVK led by actor C. Joseph Vijay made a historic debut in Tamil Nadu, becoming the first non-Dravidian Chief Minister. The Congress faces an internal challenge in Kerala with multiple candidates vying for the Chief Minister position. **Amit Shah**, Home Minister, is likely to gain further influence within the BJP as it continues its expansion across regions and social groups.  The results suggest a potential realignment of the Opposition, opening opportunities for the Congress to consolidate and galvanize support against the BJP.

recent_articles.title: With defeat in Kerala, Left out of power for first time since 1977 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Communist Party of India (Marxist)** [CPI(M)] lost the Kerala Assembly election, marking the first time since 1977 that they are not in power in any state.  **Rahul Gandhi**, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, accused the CPI(M) of collaborating with the BJP, a claim the party's general secretary **M.A. Baby** dismissed as a "deliberate" and "distorted" attempt to damage its reputation.

recent_articles.title: With defeat in Kerala, Left out of power for first time since 1977 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Communist Party of India (Marxist)** [CPI(M)] has lost its power in Kerala for the first time since 1977, marking a significant setback for the party.  **Rahul Gandhi**, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, accused the CPI(M) of colluding with the BJP during the campaign. **M.A. Baby**, the CPI(M)'s general secretary, refuted these accusations, stating they were intended to damage the party's image and that the CPI(M) supports all sections of society regardless of religion or caste.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal election results: Split in Muslim votes spells doom for Trinamool Congress - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Trinamool Congress** lost power in the 2026 Assembly elections due to a split in the Muslim vote bank, which favored the BJP and its candidates.  Several factors contributed to this shift, including discontent among Muslim voters over issues such as temple construction and lack of development in minority-dominated areas. The **Left Front**, **Congress**, and **AJUP** also benefited from this division, securing seats in Malda and Murshidabad districts where the Muslim population is significant.  The BJP's success was particularly pronounced in these areas with a majority of Hindu voters.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal election results: Split in Muslim votes spells doom for Trinamool Congress - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Trinamool Congress** lost power in the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections due to a split in the Muslim vote bank.  A combination of factors, including discontent over development and alleged lack of support for restoring voter names, led voters to choose alternative parties like the Left Front, Congress, and the Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP). The BJP benefited from this split, winning or leading in several seats with large Muslim populations.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: P. Rajeeve fails to survive anti-incumbency wave in Kalamassery - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **V.E. Abdul Gafoor**, of the **Indian Union Muslim League (IUML)**, won the Kalamassery constituency seat in Kerala, defeating outgoing Industries Minister **P. Rajeeve** of the **Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)]**.  Gafoor secured a significant victory with 80,606 votes compared to Rajeeve's 64,294. The LDF, which had pinned its hopes on Rajeeve's performance as a minister, suffered setbacks across several municipalities in the region.  Rajeeve conceded defeat and acknowledged the anti-incumbency wave affecting the Left camp.
